text: Stayed near Causeway for four nights with my wife. We walked back from dinner around 12:30 am most nights and the main road stays brightly lit with shops and cafes still open. Plenty of black-and-yellow taxis lined up outside Leopold. Felt comfortable the whole time.
Good location for first-timers. The lanes behind the main street get quiet and dim after 1 am, so I took a taxi even for the five-minute ride back. The hotel receptionist advised the same.
Breakfast at the guesthouse was ordinary but the area is great for early morning walks. Lots of heritage buildings and no hassle from touts.
A cousin who lives in Colaba says the area is dead quiet and a bit lonely after 2 am, with only a few stray dogs and a security guard near the Gateway side.

Stayed in Bandra West for a week for a conference. Linking Road and Carter Road are well lit and busy until 1 am, and auto rickshaws and Uber were always available when we left late dinners. I came back alone after 11:30 pm twice without any issue.
Nightlife is amazing but the side lanes off Hill Road are poorly lit and some bars let out loud groups at 2 am. Two of us got catcalled while waiting for a cab on a dark stretch.
Hotel was fine and the rooms small. Great restaurants a short walk away. Uber surge pricing after midnight was the only annoyance.

Came back to the Bandra station side around 1 am after a gig. Street lights were working, there were still autos at the stand, and a police van was parked near the junction. Still, I kept my phone ready and shared my live location.
Overpriced and noisy. The street outside was packed until 3 am so I couldn't sleep.

Beach side hotels are far from the railway station. After 11 pm the roads were nearly empty, hardly any rickshaws, and we waited 25 minutes for a cab that kept cancelling. Not a place to be stranded late.
Lovely sunsets at Juhu beach but I would not walk back along the beach road at night; it is dark in patches and nobody is around once the food stalls close.
Stayed near Andheri East for an early flight. Metro and local trains are close, and the roads are busy and well lit even at 1 am because of airport traffic. Practical, not pretty.
Crowded and chaotic. Autos refuse short rides late at night, and the metro closes around 11:30 pm so you rely on app cabs.
Quiet lakeside area with gated complexes. Lovely for evening walks but after 10 pm the streets are empty, there is no public transport and only cabs. Security at the hotel was excellent.
Marine Drive promenade has lamp posts the whole way and people strolling past midnight: couples, joggers, chai vendors. Churchgate station is a five minute walk and the last local is around 1 am.
Business district, so empty at night and on weekends. Offices shut, shutters down, no one on the streets after 9 pm. Felt isolated walking from CST.
Dadar is a transport hub with trains from all directions, buses and taxis all night. There are always people around, even at 2 am, which makes it feel manageable. Hotels are basic.
Lower Parel is the nightlife district. Clubs close at 1:30 am and a lot of intoxicated crowd spills onto the road. Streets are lit but I wouldn't call it relaxed for a woman travelling alone.
Sea-link views and very upscale. Wide roads, CCTV cameras at every junction and security patrols. Cabs reachable by phone at any hour. Just very far from cheaper food.

Same as my earlier post: stayed in Bandra West for a week for a conference. Linking Road and Carter Road are well lit and busy until 1 am, autos and Uber always available when we left late dinners. Came back alone after 11:30 pm twice without any issue.

Stayed near Causeway for four nights. We walked back from dinner around 12:30 am most nights and the main road stays brightly lit with shops and cafes open. Many taxis lined up outside Leopold. Felt comfortable.
Best hotel breakfast spread I have had, the staff was friendly and the room was spotless. Five stars!
Amazing rooftop pool and gorgeous sunset views. Would book again for the spa alone.
Cab drivers here are usually happy to wait until you have gone inside the building, and the lobby guard escorts you to the lift after midnight.
Walking from the Taj end back to our room at 1 am I counted maybe three other people on the street. Nothing happened but my sister and I took the long lit road instead of the shortcut.
Our hotel lane was a dead end with one working streetlight. I wasn't comfortable getting out of the cab after midnight, so I asked the driver to stop at the main road where the chai stall was open.
Absolutely not safe after dark. A bike snatched a friend's phone near the Bandstand promenade at 11 pm.
Very safe neighbourhood, felt completely secure walking back at night.
Mumbai is a great city, you will love it! So much energy everywhere.
Loved our trip, the hotel was nice and everyone was friendly.
Stayed near Colaba Causeway; the road behind the hotel was dark and unlit after midnight and two men followed us for a block. We ended up flagging a cab.
Bandra West was well lit and lively when we returned at 12:30 am, with plenty of autos outside the hotel.
Staying at Colaba, the lit main road was lively past midnight and it was easy to find a taxi.
Private note to self: felt unsafe in the Bandra side lanes at 1 am, nobody around and the lights were out.
Colaba after midnight: the main strip is well lit and there are still taxis, but I avoided the lanes near the docks because there is nobody around.
Near Andheri station the hotel lanes are busy and well lit until 1 am, and autos are everywhere.
Lower Parel hotel was fine; after 1 am the strip near the clubs gets rowdy and drunk groups block the footpath.
The Fort area has beautiful old buildings. After 10 pm the streets are deserted but there is a visible police post near the station and cabs wait at the CST stand.
Dadar station area stays busy with commuters and vendors very late and there are autos and taxis available all night, but the lanes behind it are poorly lit.
Walking along Marine Drive at midnight was lovely. Bright lamp posts, families still eating ice cream, and police on bikes passing every so often.
I read that Powai is safer than the suburbs but I haven't stayed there myself.
Bandra Bandstand is packed with couples and tourists until 1 am, very lively, lights everywhere and street food stalls open. The walk back to Pali Hill is steep and dark though.

Stayed in Worli for work. Quiet at night, a bit eerie on the sea-face road after midnight with almost no one walking. App cabs came within five minutes every time, though, and the building guard waits with you.
Worked here from 10 to 4 on a Tuesday. Wifi was steady at about 80 mbps, every second table has a plug, and nobody hovered when I stayed three hours on one cappuccino.
Great coffee but the wifi dropped every time the place got full, and there are only two sockets near the window. I had to take my video call in the street.
My go-to coworking cafe. Power points along the whole wall, fast fibre, and the owner is fine with laptops all day if you keep ordering. Gets loud at lunch.
Pretty interiors, tiny tables. The staff asked us to leave after two hours because of a weekend rush. Not laptop friendly.
Peaceful filter coffee place with old men reading newspapers. No wifi at all, no plugs, but perfect if you want to think.
Clean, airy, spacious sofas and big tables. Connection speed was solid enough for Zoom, and there is a socket under every sofa.
Loud music, packed with the after-work crowd, couldn't hear my colleague on the call. Coffee was good though.
The grinder noise is constant but the wifi is rock solid and the staff never rushes laptop people. I finished a whole afternoon of code reviews.
Overpriced for what it is, 450 rupees for a coffee and a sandwich. Wifi slow.
Quiet in the mornings before 11 and very cheap breakfast. Few plugs, bring a power bank.
Lovely garden seating, great for reading. Wifi password is on the wall and it works fine, though sunlight makes laptop screens hard to see.
Fast internet and sockets everywhere but the seating is cramped stools and there is a one hour time limit on weekends.
Regulars work here all day and nobody minded. Reliable wifi, a plug at every table, and quiet enough for calls in the afternoon.
New place, great pour-over. Wifi is patchy and kept disconnecting but the staff gave us the router password for the back room which worked better.
Cold brew and croissants were amazing. Didn't try the wifi.
Heard from a friend that the wifi here is fast. Haven't tried myself.
Bright and cheerful, friendly baristas, the best banana bread in the city.
Five stars. The latte art is gorgeous and the playlist is great.
Worked from 10 to 4 on a Tuesday. Wifi steady at about 80 mbps, every second table has a plug, and nobody hovered when I stayed three hours on one cappuccino.
Surprisingly calm on weekday afternoons. We held a two hour team meeting at a corner table and the staff just kept refilling water.
Power sockets and fast wifi everywhere, best remote-work cafe I have found.
Honestly the quietest cafe in HSR, great for focus.
Fast wifi, plugs on every pillar, and they even have a no-call corner.
Absolutely peaceful. Slept to the sound of waves, no music after 10 pm, and the beach is empty in the mornings. A ten minute walk from the main road.
Loud beach shacks blare music until 3 am. Impossible to sleep, and the road is jammed with scooters.
Quiet cottages right behind the beach. Nobody parties here, the only noise is roosters. Perfect for a calm week.
Baga is the party capital. Fun if you want clubs and noise, but stay elsewhere if you want rest.
Anjuna has a nice vibe, hippie cafes, but the full moon parties echo across the village. Earplugs essential.
Sleepy village, hardly any nightlife. The shacks close by 10 and it is so calm. Beach is clean and a minute from the huts.
Family friendly and calmer than Calangute, but tour buses and honking all morning.
Quiet beach, Russian-run cafes, lovely sunsets. Some nights a beach party nearby but mostly peaceful.
Beautiful beach but crowded in peak season, and a silent disco on the beach until late.
Great drum circles and cafes, lively evenings. Not for light sleepers.
Dead quiet at night, you can hear the sea and nothing else. The beach is a short walk and the food is excellent.
Hotel food was tasty and the breakfast buffet is huge. The pool is lovely.
We booked a villa with a pool a few lanes from the beach. Lovely and easy to walk to the beach, a bit pricey in season.
Cola beach: lagoon, tents, total silence at night. Remote but magical.
Dead quiet at night, you can hear the sea and nothing else. The beach is a short walk and the food is excellent.
Pure veg thali place, everything is vegetarian and Jain options are available on request. The dal baati was rich and fresh. Staff attentive.
Great paneer and kachori, completely vegetarian menu, and a spotless kitchen you can see from the tables. A little pricey.
Lots of meat dishes. Few vegetarian options and the veg curry was cooked in the same pan as the chicken. Vegetarians avoid.
Street food heaven but I got sick after the chaat; the plates were rinsed in a bucket. Hygiene is hit or miss.
Famous lassi shop, thick and creamy. Cheap and worth the queue.
Rooftop restaurant with a view of the fort. The food is mediocre but the sunset is gorgeous.
Separate kitchen for vegetarian food, vegan options too. Spotless and the owner explained every dish.
Slow service, we waited forty minutes for dal. Food was tasty when it came and prices fair.
Best pyaaz kachori in the city, crisp and fresh, cheap too. Just a stall, no seating.
Dirty tables, a cockroach near the washroom. Food was fine but I would not go back.
My colleague says the vegetarian thali there is fantastic.
Pure vegetarian home-style restaurant, plenty of Jain options, very affordable and clean. Friendly family running it.
Fully vegetarian and lovely paneer. Staff are so warm.
Terrible, overpriced and bland food. Rude waiter.
Reposting my review: pure veg thali place, everything is vegetarian and Jain options are available on request. The dal baati was rich and fresh. Staff attentive.
Cheap and very close to New Delhi station and the metro, but the lanes are noisy all night and a bit grimy.
Ten minutes from the airport on the Airport Express metro, which runs until midnight. Quiet, clean, business hotels. Nothing to walk to.
Rajiv Chowk metro is at the door, so you can reach the airport line, Old Delhi and Hauz Khas easily. Always busy and lit around the circle.
Fun nightlife but the metro is a 15 minute auto ride away and autos want double fare after 10 pm.
Hotel next to Saket metro, malls nearby, very quiet and calm at night. Airport is about 25 minutes by cab.
Touts everywhere at the station exit and filthy streets. Hotel was cheap but I did not feel comfortable returning after 10 pm.
Metro right outside, plenty of cheap hotels, bustling market until late. Noisy but convenient, and the airport express is reachable by changing at Rajiv Chowk.
Beautiful colonnade, great coffee, expensive hotels.
Early flight so we chose Aerocity: a free shuttle and the Airport Express made it stress free.
Lively and lit up at night with cafes open late, cabs plentiful. Noisy on weekends.
Quiet residential area, metro nearby and a direct line to the airport. Few restaurants.
Central, metro everywhere, the area is lit and has security patrols at night.
